title: Software Engineering Fundamentals
summary: Build, debug, and deploy real software before adding LLMs, as the engineering base for everything that follows.
outcome: Ship a real, tested, containerized web service without any AI in the product, and use a coding agent with disciplined verification while building it.

project.title: Ship a No-AI REST Service
deliverables: Build a complete app with Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Git, Docker and deployment, with no LLM dependency in the product
Pick a small, realistic domain (tasks, bookmarks, expenses, inventory, notes, support tickets)
Implement multiple REST endpoints with validated schemas and persistent CRUD
Integrate at least one external API, using async where it fits
Handle validation failures, missing resources, external-service errors and unexpected errors cleanly
Add automated tests, env-var configuration and useful logging
Keep a clean Git repo with a README covering setup and usage
Package with Docker and deploy to a public URL
Verify the deployed API with OpenAPI docs, curl or an API client
Use a coding agent for meaningful parts of the build and review every diff before accepting
Validate generated code with tests, type checks, linting, logs and manual calls
Explain the architecture and key code paths without the agent
Document one AI failure: what it proposed, why it was wrong, how you caught it, and the lesson

modules.title: Python for AI Engineering

topics.d: Functions, classes, modules, comprehensions, exceptions and standard-library utilities.
Choosing among lists, tuples, sets, dicts, iterators and generators.
Type hints, dataclass/Pydantic-style models and static analysis for explicit interfaces.
References, scope, exceptions, context managers and common Python pitfalls.
Files, paths, environment variables, JSON, CSV and basic serialization.
async/await for concurrent network and API calls without blocking.
Virtual environments, pyproject.toml and lockfiles with uv.
Structuring larger programs into modules and packages.
pytest basics, stack traces, logs and breakpoints.

modules.outcome: Build a small multi-file Python app that is typed, tested, dependency-managed and makes concurrent API calls.

modules.title: The Web: HTTP, REST & JSON

topics.d: URL, method, headers, body, server processing, response and status code.
GET, POST, PUT/PATCH, DELETE and what idempotency means in practice.
Status families and common codes such as 200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500.
Headers, query and path params, request bodies, content types and cookies.
Producing, parsing, validating and transforming JSON.
Designing clean endpoints for a simple application.
API keys, bearer tokens, auth headers and keeping secrets out of URLs and clients.
Debugging APIs with curl, Postman/Bruno or Python HTTP clients.

modules.outcome: Read unfamiliar API docs, build requests by hand, interpret responses and design a sensible REST API.

modules.title: Building APIs with FastAPI

topics.d: Routes, path/query params, request bodies and response models.
Pydantic models for validation, serialization and typed I/O.
Reusable dependencies via FastAPI's DI system.
Correct status codes and consistent error payloads.
Handling exceptions so stack traces never leak to clients.
Automatic OpenAPI/Swagger docs and how schemas are derived.
When to write sync or async endpoints.
Calling HTTP services from async endpoints without stalling the server.
Lifespan events, env-var config and basic middleware.
pytest with FastAPI's TestClient.

modules.outcome: Build a documented, validated, testable API that talks to at least one external service.

modules.title: Data & Persistence Basics

topics.d: Tables, keys, relationships and basic normalization.
CRUD, filtering, sorting, grouping, joins and aggregations in PostgreSQL.
What indexes do and how query shape affects performance.

topics.t: Connecting a database to the app
topics.d: Wiring PostgreSQL into a FastAPI app with a driver or ORM.
Loading DB credentials from the environment, never from code.

modules.outcome: Build an API whose data survives restarts and supports real CRUD backed by PostgreSQL.

modules.title: Git & Collaboration

topics.d: Repositories, commits, branches, remotes, diffs and the staging area.
Branch, commit, push, open a PR, review and merge.
Useful commit messages and inspecting history.
Resolving conflicts confidently.
Excluding secrets, venvs, generated files and local config.
Purpose, install, config, run, test and API usage.
Reviews, pull requests and protected main branches.

modules.outcome: Hand your repo to another developer who can understand, run and contribute without you.

modules.title: AI-Assisted Software Development

topics.d: From autocomplete to chat assistants to agents that read, edit, run and iterate.
Directing and verifying AI work versus accepting whatever it generates.

topics.t: Explore, implement & debug with an agent
topics.d: Using a coding agent such as Claude Code to explore, change and debug a repo.
Context, generate, review diff, test, debug, review, accept.
Giving the agent only what the task needs.
Keeping conventions, commands and testing notes in a project instruction file.
Write a spec, review a plan, then let the agent change code.
Turning repeated prompts into commands and on-demand skills.
Skills for review, test generation, docs, refactoring and conventions.
Handing review, testing, debugging or research to subagents.
Connecting agents to databases, APIs and docs via MCP.
Hooks that always run formatting, linting and tests.
Packaging commands, skills, hooks and agents into plugins.
Context, specs, planning, delegation and verification carry over to other agents.

modules.tryIt: Build a small multi-file app with a coding agent: write a spec and plan, add one command or skill, one subagent, one MCP integration and one hook. Review every diff, run the tests and fix at least one thing the agent got wrong.
modules.outcome: Use a coding agent as an engineering collaborator, with planning and verification around every meaningful change.
modules.mentalModel: AI coding skill multiplies engineering fundamentals; it does not replace them.

modules.title: Containers & Deployment

topics.d: Separating the application, its environment and the host.
What images and containers are and why Docker helps reproducibility.
Build and run an image, expose ports, pass env vars safely.
Image layers, .dockerignore, container logs and common startup failures.
Packaging a FastAPI service with its config and dependencies.
Deploying to a cloud platform with a reachable URL.
Managing production config separately from local development.

modules.outcome: Containerize and deploy a local service, and debug it when production behaves differently.

modules.title: Capstone: Ship a No-AI REST Service

topics.d: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Git, Docker and deployment, without an LLM in the product.
A small but realistic domain such as tasks, bookmarks or expenses.
Multiple validated endpoints with persistent CRUD.
At least one external API, async where appropriate.
Validation, missing resources, upstream errors and unexpected errors.
Automated tests, env-var config and useful logs.
Tidy structure and a README with setup and usage.
Docker image deployed to a public URL.
Checking the live API with OpenAPI docs, curl or a client.
Use an agent for real build work; the no-AI rule is about the product.
Review every meaningful generated change as a diff.
Tests, type checks, linting, logs and manual calls.
Walk through the architecture and key paths yourself.
What the agent proposed, why it failed, how you caught it and the lesson.

modules.outcome: A real service another person can clone, run, test, call over HTTP and inspect.
